injuries.longComment: Less than 24 hours after Merzlikins was traded to the Maple Leafs, a timetable for his return to action has been provided. The 32-year-old backstop had an up and down season in 2025-26, where he posted a 14-11-3 record, a 3.39 GAA and an .883 save percentage across 30 regular-season outings. He won't be rushed into action, as the Leafs new goaltender tandem of Sergei Bobrovsky and Anthony Stolarz are still expected to handle the majority of reps between the pipes this upcoming season. However, when Merzlikins is ready to return, he's the clear No. 3 option in Toronto's organization and could still see some playing time at the NHL level if he isn't sent down to AHL Toronto.
injuries.shortComment: Merzlikins is expected to miss 4-6 months to begin the 2026-27 regular season while recovering from a shoulder injury, per Luke Fox of Sportsnet.

items.headline: Hart (undisclosed) is undergoing further evaluation after suffering an injury at Thursday's morning skate, making him questionable to play in Tuesday's home clash against the Senators, per Jesse Granger of The Athletic.
items.text: Hart was seen limping off the ice before the end of Tuesday's morning skate, where he went down with his undisclosed injury. Adin Hill will start Tuesday's clash, but the question that remains is whether the 28-year-old Hart will be healthy enough to back him up. Head coach Ryan Craig stated that Vegas needs to plan for either possibility regarding Hart, so if his status starts to lean towards missing Tuesday's outing, we could see Cameron Whitehead called up on an emergency basis.

items.headline: Hart stopped 18 of 20 shots on net in Saturday's 2-1 overtime loss to the Blue Jackets.
items.text: Despite the Golden Knights' offense leaving Hart out to dry, he also struggled in his role, allowing two goals on just 20 shots. After a strong start to the season, the 28-year-old backstop has begun to trend in the wrong direction, posting three losses in his last four outings. Overall, he now has a 4-3-1 record, a 2.76 GAA and an .889 save percentage. As long as Vegas can quickly put their three-game losing streak behind them, he will remain in the No. 2 goalie conversation in fantasy. However, fantasy managers that can roster at least three goalies should have a backup plan in place if Hart's struggles persist.

items.headline: Hart will protect the road goal versus the Blue Jackets on Saturday, Mark Scheig of The Hockey Writers reports.
items.text: Hart struggled in his last start, allowing six goals on 21 shots against the Lightning on Tuesday. He'll have a prime chance to bounce back Saturday, as the Blue Jackets are off to a rough start. They've scored just 10 goals over their last five games.

items.headline: Desharnais underwent a successful appendectomy surgery Thursday and is expected to miss 4-6 weeks.
items.text: Desharnais had appeared in each of the Capitals' first nine games of the regular season, and he recorded no goals, three assists, 22 hits, 14 blocked shots and 11 PIM while averaging 19:25 of ice time. However, he's now slated to be sidelined until at least mid-to-late November while recovering from his appendectomy. Dylan McIlrath is a candidate to see increased playing time over the next several weeks, while it wouldn't be surprising to see the Capitals place Desharnais on injured reserve in order to call up an additional defenseman.
